record: As a candidate for governor, Jackson released an 'Agency over AI' plan covering data center costs and power, protections for workers, environmental oversight and transparency on state government use of AI.
grade_reason: The only AI remarks found in Jackson's own words treat AI as a question of who benefits, who pays and whether tech billionaires decide, without acknowledging catastrophic risk. A reporter's paraphrase that he said the AI race should slow down or stop is not his own words and does not change the grade.
notes: WEB SEARCH DID NOT RUN. All four general web searches I attempted were refused because the shared search budget was used up: (1) "Troy Jackson" Maine Senate artificial intelligence superintelligence; (2) Bangor Daily News Maine politicians AI extinction warnings "Troy Jackson" September 2026; (3) "Troy Jackson" "AI safety" Maine Senate candidate; (4) site:jacksonformaine.com artificial intelligence. The brief's required searches on extinction or existential risk, pause or slowdown or moratorium, and China agreement or treaty were therefore never run either. This result rests only on pages opened directly and on three newspaper site searches, so it is much weaker than a normal run and should be redone when search is available. Pages opened and read (through a page-reading tool that summarises, so I did not see raw page text): jacksonformaine.com home page, /priorities, /troy-at-a-glance and /news (153 press release titles from 27 July to 3 November 2026; I read titles only, not the releases themselves). None mentions AI, technology companies or data centers; the 11 listed priorities contain nothing on AI. Bangor Daily News, 16 September 2026 (updated 22 September), by Benjamin Kail, "How Susan Collins and other Maine politicians are responding to dire AI warnings": opened. It contains no direct quote from Jackson himself. It paraphrases him as treating AI regulation as a worker-protection issue and warning that "billionaires" will profit while ordinary Mainers bear the costs, and says he would welcome data centers only with union jobs and protection of natural resources. It quotes campaign spokesperson Cheyenne Gallivan (not Jackson), in part: "Troy Jackson believes we need common-sense AI regulations that give workers a seat at the table" and "He knows that if left unchecked, the billionaires benefiting from artificial intelligence will only get richer" (these are excerpts of longer sentences as relayed by the reading tool; verify against the page before any use). According to the reading tool, the article does not show Jackson or his campaign addressing extinction, loss of control, superintelligence, a pause or China, even though the article was prompted by a researcher's warning that AI "could kill us all". I left all of this out of statements because spokesperson words and paraphrases are not his own words. Bangor Daily News, 19 August 2026, "Susan Collins takes cautious line on data centers opposed by most Mainers": opened; again no direct Jackson quote; an unnamed campaign spokesperson is quoted on data centers creating union jobs, and the article paraphrases a pledge by Jackson to regulate data centers within 100 days of taking office; nothing on risks from AI itself. Not checked: the four debates with Collins (6-15 October 2026), his Maine Calling interview on Maine Public (1 October 2026, https://www.mainepublic.org/show/maine-calling/2026-10-01/candidate-interviews-rick-bennett-troy-jackson), town halls, television interviews, candidate questionnaires, and his record in the Maine Senate; any of these could contain AI remarks. Could not open: congress.gov search for the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (HTTP 403) and Maine Morning Star site search (HTTP 403). On the two events in the brief: Jackson was a candidate, not a senator, in September 2026, so he could not have signed the 23 September letter or co-sponsored the bill; I found no source showing him commenting on either. Identity: every page relied on identifies him as the Democratic Senate nominee in Maine and former state Senate president, so there is no confusion with other people named Troy Jackson.
